key_insight: The paper introduces a recommendation model that exploits the structured nature of psychometric data (e.g., item/scale and latent-trait relationships) to generate clinically useful, transparent recommendations for gerontological primary care. This yields actionable suggestions while keeping the decision logic interpretable to clinicians.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between black‑box recommenders and clinical needs by producing recommendations from scarce, sensitive psychometric data in a way that clinicians can understand, trust, and act on safely.
method: Represent psychometric assessments using their latent structure (e.g., item/scale relationships and latent traits) to create compact patient profiles.
Map profiles to recommendations with inherently interpretable models (e.g., sparse rules/trees or linear models constrained for transparency) that expose which items or traits drive each suggestion.
Validate the approach on gerontological primary care data, measuring recommendation relevance, uncertainty, and clinician-facing interpretability metrics.
impact: Provides a practical template for building recommenders for sensitive healthcare domains where interpretability, limited data, and safety are paramount—helping ML practitioners design models that clinicians can inspect and trust.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: psychometric survey → latent-trait extraction → interpretable model → recommendation + explanation
Heatmap or loadings chart showing item-to-trait relationships to illustrate how psychometric structure is used
Flowchart or rule-sets mapping patient profile ranges to concrete care recommendations (easy for clinicians to read)
Example patient card: raw responses, derived trait scores, recommended action, and the top contributing items (explanation overlay)
paper_title: An Interpretable Recommendation Model for Psychometric Data, With an Application to Gerontological Primary Care
paper_authors: Andre Paulino de Lima, Paula Castro, Suzana Carvalho Vaz de Andrade, Rosa Maria Marcucci, Ruth Caldeira de Melo
